editorNote: A light Tuesday on verifiable material: Bitcoin's oldest overhang gets another year, and Alphabet heads toward earnings with heavy AI spending as the central question. Only items we could source are reported; no view on direction is offered.

stories.headline: Mt. Gox pushes its creditor repayment deadline to October 2027, with about 34,000 BTC still undistributed
stories.summary: Trustee Nobuaki Kobayashi moved the Base, Early Lump-Sum and Intermediate repayment deadline from Oct. 31, 2026 to Oct. 31, 2027, in a notice dated Oct. 16 and with court permission. The estate still holds 34,388 BTC (about $2.8 billion), and no distributions have been made since June.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the fourth one-year extension; the trustee cites creditors who have not completed required procedures and gives no timetable for further payouts.

sourceLinks.title: Mt. Gox Pushes Repayment Deadline to 2027 With $2.8B in Bitcoin Still to Distribute - Decrypt

stories.headline: Alphabet is expected to report Q3 results on Oct. 28, after a quarter of record cloud growth and negative free cash flow
stories.summary: Calendar sites list Oct. 28 as the expected date, though some mark it unconfirmed. In Q2, revenue was $119.8 billion, Google Cloud grew 82% to $24.8 billion, 2026 capex guidance rose to $195–205 billion, and one report put free cash flow at -$5.9 billion.
stories.whyItMatters: Coverage frames the open question as whether heavy AI spending returns fast enough; Q2 shares fell after the report.
